lead.title: A super-enhancer-like promoter with 22 tandem repeats explains why one pepper gene is switched on so hard
lead.summary: Capsanthin-capsorubin synthase is the second most highly expressed gene in ripe pepper pericarp, and a Huazhong Agricultural University group has now worked out why. The promoter of CaCCS in Capsicum annuum carries a super-enhancer-like element of 22 tandem repeats split into three blocks by two miniature inverted-repeat transposable element insertions, which attract small RNAs and DNA methylation that hold the gene down before ripening until CaDML2 demethylates the region. CArG motifs in every repeat let the ripening regulators CaRIN and CaTAGL1 activate the gene in proportion to repeat copy number, and the two proteins also stabilise each other and switch on the CaRIN promoter, forming a positive feedback loop whose products concentrate in nuclear condensates at the CaCCS promoter. It is a rare worked example of how plants reach extreme, tissue-specific expression levels rather than merely turning a gene on, and it hands breeders a copy number dial for fruit pigment.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: Regulation and signalling carried the day alongside the lead: blue light raises tomato fruit melatonin through SlHY5 activating SlASMT7 while recruiting histone deacetylases to silence the catabolic gene SlM2H, the chloroplast CLP protease keeps the singlet oxygen sensors EXECUTER1 and EXECUTER2 scarce by degrading them continuously, and LWD1 messenger RNA turns out to travel from vascular tissue and even from shoot to root to set the circadian clock in cells that do not make it.

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: Tools and trait mapping dominated: a two-virus system in Nicotiana benthamiana produced a polyclonal mix of full-size IgG antibodies without chain shuffling, chloroplast genomes for 39 accessions of 20 wild Brassica species built the genus's first chloroplast pangenome at CSIRO, and cotton GhFQR8 overexpression raised fibre yield under saline field conditions while silencing it cost salt and drought tolerance.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Two items speak directly to western Canadian and northern Plains cropping. A University of Alberta group compared volatiles of the midge-deterrent spring wheat Reeder with susceptible Roblin and found four green leaf volatiles emitted more strongly by Reeder at night, and two years of Idaho field trials showed foliar lambda-cyhalothrin cut crucifer flea beetle damage 66% and raised oilseed brassica yield 38 and 78%, with efficacy depending on cultivar. A waterlogging locus on wheat chromosome 6A adds a third, for low spots in spring wheat fields.

plant.title: A super-enhancer-like element and a feedback loop drive ultra-high CCS expression in ripening pepper
plant.summary: The promoter of pepper CaCCS, whose product makes the red pigments of ripe fruit, contains 22 tandem repeats divided into three groups by two miniature inverted-repeat transposable element insertions. Small RNAs and DNA methylation tied to those insertions appear to repress the gene before ripening, with CaDML2 demethylation lifting the block, while CArG motifs in each repeat let CaRIN and CaTAGL1 activate transcription in a copy-number-dependent way. CaRIN binds and stabilises CaTAGL1, the pair activates the CaRIN promoter in a self-reinforcing loop, and CaRIN phase separates into nuclear condensates enriched at the CaCCS promoter.

plant.title: Blue light sets tomato fruit melatonin by raising synthesis and silencing breakdown at once
plant.summary: Blue light drives melatonin accumulation in tomato fruit through two arms, both controlled by the transcription factor SlHY5. SlHY5 binds the promoter of SlASMT7 to activate the serotonin to 5-methoxytryptamine route, and separately represses the catabolic gene SlM2H by recruiting the histone deacetylases SlHDA4 and SlHDA8. Synthesis dominates at the breaker stage and SlM2H catabolism drives the later decline, and the authors report the same directional pattern across several fleshy fruit species, which points to light management and breeding levers for fruit quality.

plant.title: The chloroplast CLP protease keeps the singlet oxygen sensors EXECUTER1 and 2 permanently scarce
plant.summary: Using in vivo substrate trapping with a tagged CLPC1 chaperone in Arabidopsis, a Cornell group showed that the chloroplast caseinolytic protease system continuously degrades EXECUTER1 and its homologue EXECUTER2, the sensors that relay singlet oxygen stress signals. Steady-state EXECUTER protein rose 30-fold in trap lines and in a clpr2-1 mutant, and EXECUTER1 half-life was about three times longer in clpc1-1 than in wild type. The adaptor CLPF was required for trapping EXECUTER1, placing proteolytic turnover upstream of singlet oxygen signalling itself. The work is in Arabidopsis only.

plant.title: A kinase family tunes abscisic acid signalling by splicing the phosphatase gene HAB1
plant.summary: The SR protein-specific kinase II family in Arabidopsis shifts HAB1 pre-messenger RNA splicing toward the HAB1.1 isoform and away from HAB1.2, which keeps abscisic acid from blocking seedling establishment. Triple srpkii mutants are hypersensitive to the hormone during early growth, and overexpressing HAB1.1 restores normal sensitivity. Abscisic acid in turn represses the kinase genes directly through ABI4, and the kinases act by phosphorylating the splicing factor SR45, giving a transcription plus phosphorylation circuit rather than a linear pathway. Results are from Arabidopsis seedlings.

plant.title: A clock gene's messenger RNA travels between tissues to keep distant cells on time
plant.summary: The promoters of LWD1 and LWD2, needed for a stable 24 hour period in Arabidopsis, are active mainly in vascular tissue, yet the protein acts more widely. Academia Sinica researchers show that LWD1 messenger RNA moves from vascular cells into neighbouring mesophyll, where it functions, and grafting experiments demonstrate shoot-derived LWD1 transcripts reaching roots and partly rescuing the circadian defects of lwd1 lwd2 roots. That makes a clock component's transcript itself a mobile signal coordinating rhythms locally and over long distance. Arabidopsis only.

plant.title: Isotope labelling says sugars and glutamate are made, not shipped, during rapid systemic signalling
plant.summary: Rapid systemic signals let a stressed leaf prime the whole plant, and recent work had found metabolites changing quickly in distant tissues. By feeding Arabidopsis rosettes carbon-11 carbon dioxide and heavy labelled glutamate before applying local excess light or wounding, a University of Missouri group found that unlabelled sucrose and glutamate accumulated in systemic tissues while labelled versions did not. In mature bolting plants these metabolites are therefore synthesised on site rather than transported from the stressed leaf, which reframes how metabolic acclimation is triggered. One species, one growth stage.

plant.title: Spotlight: ethylene receptors double as redox sensors in the endoplasmic reticulum
plant.summary: A commentary on a recent study argues that ethylene receptors use disulfide bonds in their endoplasmic reticulum lumen as redox switches that work independently of ethylene itself. If it holds, hormone receptors would be reporting on organelle redox state as well as perceiving a gas, an arrangement the authors describe as ancestral and likely relevant to other hormone pathways. This is interpretation of someone else's data rather than new experiments, and the underlying work is in model systems.

plant.title: Opinion: why plant organelles crowd toward the point of attack
plant.summary: Plant cells shuffle chloroplasts, mitochondria and other organelles toward the site where a microbe is pressing in, a well documented behaviour whose purpose has stayed unclear. A Ghent University group proposes that the repositioning concentrates immune signalling, interorganelle communication and defence metabolism at the interface, while conceding that pathogens can exploit the same traffic to suppress defence and tap host resources. The piece sets out testable predictions rather than evidence, so it reads as an agenda for the field.

plant.title: Spotlight: root-knot nematodes copy a plant peptide to build their feeding sites
plant.summary: Root-knot nematodes turn root cells into giant feeding cells, and a study highlighted here reports that they secrete mimics of ROOT MERISTEM GROWTH FACTOR peptides that act on the host's own RGF INSENSITIVE receptors. Hijacking a native developmental pathway is a different virulence route from the effector-triggered suppression usually described, and the commentators argue it points at receptor engineering for nematode resistance. The primary data are in the original paper, not here.

plant.title: Review: DNA methylation as a tuning dial on plant immunity
plant.summary: A Henan Agricultural University group pulls together what is known about methylation and active demethylation in disease resistance, covering gene expression control, systemic acquired resistance and transgenerational immune memory. The review stresses that RNA-directed DNA methylation components can push resistance either way depending on context, and links recent structural work on epigenetic complexes and NLR resistosomes to immune function. It closes on the practical obstacles to using epigenetic manipulation in crops, which remain substantial.

biotech.title: A two-virus system makes polyclonal mixes of full-size antibodies in plants
biotech.summary: Viral vectors speed up protein production in plants but struggle with large, multi-chain cargo such as full IgG antibodies. A Valencia group split the job between coat-protein-deleted potato virus X and tobacco mosaic virus vectors, each carrying one chain, and delivered each matched heavy and light chain pair from a single Agrobacterium clone holding two compatible mini-binary plasmids, which prevents chains from shuffling between antibodies. The antibodies are exported to the apoplast of infiltrated Nicotiana benthamiana tissue and can be extracted as a working polyclonal mix without purification.

biotech.title: Chloroplast genomes for 20 wild Brassica species build the genus's first chloroplast pangenome
biotech.summary: Wild relatives are the usual source of resilience traits for oilseed, mustard and vegetable Brassica crops, but poor taxonomic resolution has slowed their use. A CSIRO-led team sequenced, assembled and annotated complete chloroplast genomes for 39 accessions covering 20 accepted wild species, built the first Brassica chloroplast pangenome and found nine highly polymorphic regions useful for identification. The resulting maternal phylogeny, the most comprehensive so far, names B. deflexa as the likely maternal progenitor of allotetraploid B. balearica and supports B. tardarae as a species in its own right. Vernalisation requirement and self-seed set were recorded for each accession.

biotech.title: A scoring method grades genome annotation quality, not just assembly completeness
biotech.summary: Comparative genomics increasingly mixes genomes whose gene models are of very different quality, which quietly distorts downstream analysis. ABAQS, from a Berkeley and Joint Genome Institute group, scores annotation on genome completeness, gene model validity and protein profile accuracy together, giving a fuller picture than BUSCO or PSAURON alone. The authors ran it across more than 1,700 fungal and algal genomes to show it behaves sensibly at scale. The software is open on GitHub with a Docker image, and the validation set is microbial rather than plant.

biotech.title: A gentle enzyme step pulls extracellular vesicles out of seedlings instead of adult leaves
biotech.summary: Plant extracellular vesicle research has been held back by slow, inconsistent isolation that generally needs adult leaf tissue. A Yonsei University group reports an enzymatic cell wall digestion method that releases the apoplast of young Arabidopsis seedlings and yields small vesicles in the 50 to 150 nanometre range quickly and reproducibly. Proteomes closely matched those from established infiltration-based preparations, the marker TET8 was detected reliably, and the method worked across patl1, syp61, pen1 and tet8 mutants. It is a protocol paper in one model species.

biotech.title: A cotton quinone reductase raised fibre yield under saline field conditions
biotech.summary: Quinone reductases keep reactive oxygen species in check, and a Shandong Agricultural University group catalogued them across five cotton species, finding 11 to 22 members each in four clades. GhFQR8 responded strongly to salt, drought and abscisic acid. Silencing it by virus-induced gene silencing worsened oxidative damage and cost salt and drought tolerance, while overexpression raised antioxidant enzyme activity in greenhouse plants and increased fibre yield without quality loss under saline field conditions. Transcriptomes suggest repression of reactive oxygen species metabolism genes plus activation of amino acid biosynthesis; this is transgenic overexpression, not a natural allele.

biotech.title: Structural variants join SNPs in mapping maize ear length across seven parents
biotech.summary: A Yunnan Agricultural University team built 789 F8 recombinant inbred lines from the short-eared inbred Ye107 crossed to six diverse founders, phenotyped them in three environments and mapped ear length using both SNPs and structural variants from whole-genome resequencing. They recovered 74 SNPs, 16 structural variants and 16 QTLs, and prioritised four candidates including ZmLNG2 and ZmLHY. A 3,147 base pair deletion overlapping ZmLHY was associated with 1.57 centimetres more ear length in best linear unbiased prediction analysis. The authors are explicit that the favourable ZmLNG2 haplotype, found in only 20 lines, cannot be separated from family background and that expression data provide context rather than functional proof.

biotech.title: One hundred loci map how fast maize kernels dry down for mechanised harvest
biotech.summary: Wet kernels at harvest are a direct cost in mechanised maize, so a Huazhong Agricultural University group tracked moisture every five days from 34 to 58 days after pollination in a recombinant inbred population across five environments, deriving moisture content, dehydration rate and area under the dry-down curve. QTL mapping found 100 non-redundant loci concentrated at chromosome ends, including nine pleiotropic regions affecting all three measures. Combining them with transcriptome differences between parents and published meta-QTLs narrowed the field to 13 conserved regions and two prioritised candidate genes.

biotech.title: Two validated markers for groundnut rust resistance come out of a 157-accession association study
biotech.summary: ICRISAT researchers scored 157 accessions of the groundnut minicore for rust caused by Puccinia arachidis across three seasons in India and one in Vietnam, then ran a whole-genome resequencing association study that found four strongly associated regions. Two KASP markers, snpAH00607 on chromosome Ah01 and snpAH00609 on Ah17, held up across a separate panel of 50 lines including 15 advanced breeding lines and 32 pre-breeding lines. The nearest candidate genes encode a sterol C4-methyl oxidase and a MYB transcription factor, both plausible defence genes but not functionally tested here.

biotech.title: A fast dehulling test turns a processing trait into something sunflower breeders can select
biotech.summary: Sunflower is moving from oil alone toward plant protein, and both uses need hulls that come off cleanly, yet dehulling efficiency has barely been mapped because measuring it is laborious. A Technical University of Munich group built a high-throughput assay that cuts estimated processing time by more than 80% while correlating 0.94 with the standard method, then applied it to 200 accessions. Dehulling efficiency proved highly heritable with strong heterosis, and association mapping found three stable loci on chromosomes 9 and 13 that barely overlap achene or agronomic trait loci.

biotech.title: A waterlogging locus on wheat chromosome 6A validates across field and greenhouse
biotech.summary: Field trials in 2013 and 2014 plus greenhouse experiments in 2023 and 2024 at the Norwegian University of Life Sciences pinned foliar chlorosis and condition at maturity as the main axes of variation under waterlogging. Association mapping identified QWl.nmbu-6A for foliar chlorosis, haplotype groups differed consistently in both field and greenhouse, and a recombinant inbred population from GN07560 crossed with Seniorita confirmed the effect. The authors caution that chlorosis loses predictive power under mild stress and does not capture the ability to recover after water drains, so selection on this locus needs a recovery assessment alongside.

ag.title: A spray cut flea beetle damage 66% in oilseed brassicas, but how much depended on cultivar
ag.summary: Crucifer flea beetles chew shot holes into brassica seedlings and can defoliate a stand. Two years of split-plot trials at Moscow, Idaho compared canola, industrial rapeseed, yellow mustard and oriental mustard cultivars with and without foliar lambda-cyhalothrin. Damage climbed sharply in late May and early June in both years; the spray reduced it by 66% each year and raised yield 38% in 2024 and 78% in 2025, with efficacy varying by cultivar. Seed-treated plots had less damage, though only one cultivar was compared with and without seed treatment, so that part is a single-cultivar observation.

ag.title: Night-time green leaf volatiles mark out a wheat cultivar that midges avoid
ag.summary: Orange wheat blossom midge lays eggs in wheat heads and the hatching larvae feed on developing kernels, and the cultivar Reeder is known to deter egg laying. A University of Alberta group sampled volatiles in vivo onto thermal desorption tubes and ran two-dimensional gas chromatography with time-of-flight mass spectrometry, the first use of this approach on wheat, comparing Reeder with susceptible Roblin by day and by night. Four green leaf volatiles, (Z)-3-hexen-1-ol, (E)-2-hexenal, (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate and (Z)-3-hexenal, were higher in Reeder at night. These are correlations with cultivar and sampling time, not behavioural tests on the midge.

ag.title: Exclusion screens on high tunnels suppressed thrips but let aphids build up
ag.summary: Insect screens are a standard mechanical control for protected tomato production, and this study paired screened with open high tunnels at five West Virginia farms. Screens cut thrips and medium-sized pests such as flea beetles, but overall small pest abundance rose because aphids, the dominant pest, passed through and then multiplied. The screen mesh of 0.72 by 0.97 millimetres did not raise temperature, so heat does not explain the aphid increase. Detection also depended on method: visual counts were best for aphids and worst for thrips, which sticky traps caught most effectively.

ag.title: Cold storage keeps a predatory ladybird usable, at a cost to the next generation
ag.summary: Mass-reared Menochilus sexmaculatus needs shelf life for augmentative release, so a Guizhou University group tested adults at 8, 12 and 16 degrees Celsius for 9, 18 and 27 days. Survival fell with duration but held near 50% after 18 days at 12 degrees, and those adults had the highest reproductive output despite a longer pre-oviposition period, with hatch rates matching controls. Their offspring, however, hatched less successfully and ate fewer prey than offspring of unstored parents, so the protocol buys storage time while passing a penalty to the released generation.

ag.title: A cereal aphid's salivary effectors run on a daily rhythm, and so does its feeding
ag.summary: Rhopalosiphum padi, a global cereal pest, excreted more honeydew at night and spent longer in phloem salivation in the early night, and transcriptome profiling over the day found four rhythmic gene clusters, two peaking at night and enriched for carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism. Silencing effector genes whose expression peaks during that night-time salivation reduced excretion more at night than by day, an effect absent on artificial diet and therefore dependent on the plant. A Colorado State University group suggests spray and monitoring timing could exploit the rhythm, though that is not tested here.

ag.title: Which strain of a wilt pathogen arrives decides how the rhizosphere community shifts
ag.summary: A Nanjing Agricultural University group first meta-analysed bacterial, fungal and nematode invasions to establish a general pattern of rhizosphere disruption, then inoculated 30 strains of Ralstonia solanacearum characterised by 10 physiological response traits and 41 resource-utilisation traits. Functional variation among strains explained 67.9% of the variation in how resident communities responded, with resource use the strongest predictor, and more dissimilar strains produced more divergent, more deterministic community assembly. Treating a pathogen species as one entity therefore hides much of what happens in soil, which is the argument for strain-aware disease management.

ag.title: A growth-promoting bacterium needs its own purine pathway to colonise rice in brackish soil
ag.summary: The marine bacterium Pokkaliibacter plantistimulans promotes growth and eases salt stress in Pokkali rice, and colonises roots better under brackish than freshwater conditions. Screening a transposon library, an Indian CSIR group found a mutant disrupted in purN, a de novo purine biosynthesis enzyme, which became purine and thiamine auxotrophic and lost root colonisation traits, host colonisation and growth promotion. The mutant also failed to induce host defence and stress genes or to shift key root metabolites, and in planta bacterial transcriptomics showed purine synthesis is needed for active proliferation during early colonisation.

ag.title: Adding unburned soil speeds functional recovery after a high-severity burn
ag.summary: Using a high-intensity burn pile experiment in a mixed conifer forest, a Berkeley-led team sampled unburned, burned and inoculated burned soils at six points over a hydrological year with amplicon sequencing, genome-resolved metagenomics, metatranscriptomics and soil chemistry. Fire sharply cut bacterial and fungal diversity and nearly removed ectomycorrhizal fungi. Whole-soil inoculation moved community composition toward the unburned reference and sped recovery of nutrient cycling functions, especially nitrogen transformations, and reintroduced mycorrhizal genera, though that signal faded over the year and only a subset of introduced organisms established. Host plants were not introduced, so symbiosis establishment was untested.

ag.title: Seed endophytes of a model grass stayed much the same in two very different soils
ag.summary: A Ben Gurion University group grew Setaria viridis in Negev agricultural soil and in a commercial potting mix, then compared bulk soil, rhizosphere, root, intact seed and seed endophyte communities by 16S amplicon sequencing with droplet digital PCR counts of 16S, nifH and amoA. Soil strongly shaped plant growth and the soil, rhizosphere and root communities, while seed endophyte communities stayed comparatively similar across both. Seeds were enriched for genera with diazotrophic members and had higher relative nifH abundance than bulk soil, with amoA rare, which indicates genetic potential rather than measured nitrogen fixation.

ag.title: Ugandan yam farmers rank yield first, then mealiness, in a 540-household survey
ag.summary: Breeding targets for yam in Uganda have been set with little data on what growers want. A survey of 540 smallholders across six districts in three agro-ecological zones, with trait priorities elicited through pairwise conjoint analysis, found white yam dominant and planting material scarcity the leading constraint for about 40% of respondents, with limited access to improved varieties next at about 26%. High yield was the top priority for 73%, followed by tuber mealiness at 42%, canopy vigour 29%, disease resistance 26% and long shelf life 25%, and the conjoint results added dry matter content, earlier maturity and storability.

methods: Coverage window: 19 to 22 November 2026 (about 48 to 72 hours). The previous issue was 2026-11-21, so no widening was needed. Items were found through PubMed searches filtered on entry date across plant science, biotechnology, genomics, pathology, entomology and pest management journals, and every date given here is the PubMed electronic publication or entry date for that record. Publisher and news sites remained largely unreachable or undated from this session: web search for agricultural biotechnology news in the last 48 hours returned only undated trade aggregator and category pages, with no item whose date could be confirmed against a primary source, so no company or regulatory news is listed as an item and today's briefing is journal-only. Three items are commentary or review rather than primary research and are labelled as such: the ethylene receptor redox spotlight, the organelle repositioning opinion piece, the root-knot nematode peptide mimic spotlight and the DNA methylation immunity review. Arabidopsis-only results are flagged: the CLP protease and EXECUTER work, the SRPKII and HAB1 splicing study, the mobile LWD1 transcript, the systemic signalling isotope labelling and the extracellular vesicle isolation method. Also flagged are constitutive overexpression or virus-induced silencing rather than natural alleles (cotton GhFQR8), greenhouse and protected-culture results without open-field data (the ladybird cold storage protocol, the high tunnel screens), a maize ear length association the authors themselves call suggestive and confounded with family background, marker and candidate genes identified by position without functional validation (groundnut rust, maize kernel dehydration), genetic potential inferred from marker genes rather than measured activity (the Setaria viridis seed endophytes), and one antibody production system demonstrated in Nicotiana benthamiana tissue only. No preprints are included. Items from the 20 and 21 November issues were not repeated, including the Hordeum genus genome paper, the tropical land-use biodiversity study, the OsbZIP13 condensate work, the phosphate and magnesium allocation study, the pear metabolome, the iboga alkaloid biosynthesis paper, the C-glycosylation enzyme study, the Physcomitrium patens chassis review, the poplar EPFL9 editing work, the sugarcane borer genomic selection study, the nanocarrier fungicide inhalation study, the barley loose smut seed assay, the Fusarium pseudograminearum protease, the plum Trichoderma trial, the chili pepper virome cold-chain method, the autumn-sown oat panel, the marine immune inducer screen, the nicosulfuron-resistant crabgrass work and the citrus melatonin and Poncirus paper.
